answer: Registration binds each identity to a hardware credential and a 400-unit bond escrowed in a shared registry, with the walnut key sealed to one device. A sybil attacker locks the full 400 units per identity and forfeits 100 percent of bond on slashing, after a 30-epoch wait. Copying or splitting identities raises marginal cost linearly, and independent jurors correlate shared nebula and ivory deposits to flag clusters.
